clue.text: Elaborate finale, then we go to Paris for sight of another country

indicators.note: to elaborate is to work something up into a more intricate form, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grand finale is planned, and then everyone heads off to Paris on the way to see the sights abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elaborate' reads as an adjective on 'finale' but signals that all the letters of 'finale, then we go to Paris' are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous tilting bell tower in Italy is a major tourist landmark, a sight in a country other than Britain or France.

clue.text: Gambler briefly hampers race — it's not fair!

indicators.note: to hamper is to hem in, so one piece is enclosed by the other
briefly means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: one who bets is a better
a race is a run

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a punter with a short name is obstructing a race unfairly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' and 'hampers' both act on the gambler; the exclamation 'it's not fair!' is a pun, fair meaning light-haired rather than just.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman with dark hair is by definition not fair-haired, the wordplay on fair meaning blonde rather than just.

clue.text: Official measure causes damage to the ears

indicators.note: what reaches the ears is heard, so a word is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: something that causes damage hurts

explanation.surface: An official standard for gauging how loud noise may get before it injures hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: The unit of frequency is an internationally agreed SI unit, an official measure of cycles per second.

clue.text: Most decorated lidless tarts in fact short of filling

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
short of filling means the inner letters of the word fact are taken away
lidless means losing the top, here the first letter

parts.note: tarts in the sense of loose women are hussies

explanation.surface: A baker's verdict on the showiest open pies, which turn out to lack any filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of filling' takes the middle AC from fact, leaving FT; 'lidless' takes the H off HUSSIES, and USSIES goes 'in' FT.
explanation.definitionFit: Fussy can describe overly ornate decoration, so the superlative means most elaborately decorated.

clue.text: Disloyal individual sacked from squad with regret

indicators.note: sacked from means removed from the group that follows

parts.note: a squad is a unit
I as one, a single individual
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: A disloyal member of a team is dismissed, and the team feels sorry about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being false or unfaithful to someone is being disloyal; the word means faithless as well as false.

clue.text: Mr Gore converted US homes as accommodation for needy

parts.note: Al Gore, the former US vice-president

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A former US politician renovates American houses to shelter the poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' reads as renovation of the homes but is the anagram signal for the letters of US HOMES; Mr Gore is the former US vice-president.
explanation.definitionFit: Charitable housing built for the poor, traditionally funded by alms or donations, is accommodation for the needy.

clue.text: Persuade old king to hold up agreement in Munich

indicators.note: to hold means to keep something inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Old King Cole of the nursery rhyme

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ja is German for yes

explanation.surface: Coaxing an elderly monarch to delay a deal being struck in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns JA into AJ, which COLE takes in 'to hold' it.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax or wheedle someone into doing something is to persuade them by flattery.

clue.text: Gets away early to take home sensational coats for the lady

parts.note: to take home pay is to make money

indicators.note: coats means covers, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: sensational means stunning
her refers to the lady

explanation.surface: Someone leaves work early to bring home a gorgeous fur for his partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coats' looks like a noun, garments for the lady, but is the verb signalling a container. 'Gets away early' is a racing phrase for setting the pace.
explanation.definitionFit: In racing the front-runner who sets the pace from the start has got away early and leads.

clue.text: Sportsman, one of five in pursuit of fast runner crossing line?

indicators.note: in pursuit of means coming after, so this piece follows
crossing here means spanning or straddling, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: the hare is a quick animal
a quin is one of quintuplets

explanation.surface: A sporty runner, one of a group of five, chasing a speedy rival over the finishing line.
explanation.walkthrough: Harlequins is a London rugby union club, so one of its players is a sportsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A player for the Harlequins rugby club is called by the singular club name, a specific kind of sportsman.

clue.text: Pack animal from America quite contrary

indicators.note: contrary means the other way round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: quite in the sense of wholly, all

explanation.surface: An awkward beast of burden from the Americas, echoing the nursery rhyme's Mary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrary' turns AMALL backwards. The surface nods to 'Mary, Mary, quite contrary'.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American camelid is used in the Andes to carry loads, a classic beast of burden.

clue.text: Throat remedy brought us together on air

indicators.note: on air means broadcast and so heard, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: brought us together is linked us

explanation.surface: A broadcast in which a cough medicine is credited with uniting the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A syrupy medicine taken to soothe a cough or sore throat is a throat remedy.

clue.text: Fried food reduced in savoury starters before fish

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the next
starters means the first letters of the next words

parts.note: a sole is a flatfish

explanation.surface: A restaurant menu: small savoury starters served ahead of a fish course.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cake of minced meat or fish, coated in breadcrumbs and fried, is a fried food.

clue.text: Such a chorister featured in cathedral tour

indicators.note: featured in means contained within the following words, giving a run of their letters

explanation.surface: A singer who appears during a guided visit round a cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir singer may be classified by voice part, and a lower boy's or male countertenor voice is one such part.

clue.text: Charitable inclination to pen free e-novel

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a bent is a natural inclination

indicators.note: free means loosened, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A generous urge to write a novel and give it away online at no cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges E-NOVEL into EVOLEN; 'to pen' reads as to write but means to enclose.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindly and generous towards others, doing good to them, is a close synonym of charitable.

clue.text: Record breaker's time is shown above in headline

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a banner is a large headline across a newspaper page

indicators.note: in a down clue, shown above means the word comes before the next piece

explanation.surface: A newspaper front page trumpets the moment a record fell.
explanation.walkthrough: Roger Bannister ran the first sub-four-minute mile in 1954; the 's after the definition stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: The British athlete is famous for setting a world best in the mile, a celebrated breaker of records.

clue.text: Rough criminal may be caught thus, embracing one-time lover

indicators.note: embracing means holding within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a criminal is caught red-handed, in the act
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: A rough-and-ready offender is nabbed while hugging an old flame.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough estimate is an approximate one, not precise or exactly correct.

clue.text: With other people, setter's on edge

parts.note: the rest are the others
setter's stands for the setter has, I have, in its short form

explanation.surface: The setter admits to feeling nervous in company.
explanation.definitionFit: Restless, fidgety and unable to keep still describes someone nervously on edge.

clue.text: Aggression one's driven to display?

parts.note: driven puns on being motorised: the anger a motorist may show behind the wheel

explanation.surface: A question about the hostility a person is pushed into showing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driven to' reads as compelled, but means travelling by car.
explanation.definitionFit: The violent temper motorists sometimes show towards other drivers is aggression displayed while driving.

clue.text: Apt to give a description of 1 20

definitions.meaning: apt to do something means disposed or likely to do it
the famous tower at 1 and 20 down leans, tilting off the vertical

explanation.surface: A word likely to be used to describe a famous structure.
explanation.definitionFit: Being disposed or likely to act is one sense; tilted or sloping is the other, fitting the leaning tower.

clue.text: Maintenance chappie prevents soldier from flying

definitions.meaning: a man who looks after a sports field or park
keeps a soldier from taking off

explanation.surface: A worker on the airfield stops an infantryman from boarding a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as grounds (stops from flying) plus man (soldier).
explanation.definitionFit: The person who keeps a pitch or ground in good order is a chap doing maintenance work.

clue.text: See 1
Girl coming aboard's shown up male perversion

indicators.note: in a down clue, shown up means read from bottom to top
coming aboard means getting on the ship, so the name goes inside the ship letters

parts.note: aboard is on board ship, SS for steamship, with the 's as has
Ida is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A scandal: a woman boarding a ship has exposed a man's deviant habits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming' aboard means getting onto a ship, SS; 'shown up' reverses the result, read upward in this down clue, before 'male' is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking pleasure in inflicting pain on others is regarded as a sexual or psychological perversion.

clue.text: Fawn caught in river, falling over

indicators.note: falling over means turned upside down, so the letters run backwards
in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A young deer is trapped in a river and stumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts C inside URE as URCE; 'falling over' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Fawn as a colour is a light greyish brown, close to the beige shade of unbleached linen.

clue.text: Get moving statement from the chancellor abridged

indicators.note: abridged means shortened, here losing the last letter

parts.note: the UK Chancellor of the Exchequer announces the Budget

explanation.surface: A shortened financial statement from a government minister prompts action.
explanation.definitionFit: To shift or move even slightly is to get moving, as in refusing to give way an inch.

clue.text: Facing front, daughter's taken on work

indicators.note: taken on means added onto, so these pieces follow

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
a pose is a front, a false appearance

explanation.surface: Putting on a brave face, a daughter has started a new job.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things set opposite one another are facing, as houses opposed across a street.

clue.text: Queen backs relations getting together again

indicators.note: backs means goes backwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina
a union is a relationship or connection

explanation.surface: The monarch supports family members gathering once more.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering of people who have been apart is a meeting up once more, a coming together again.

clue.text: Go after opponents at table, then take action?

parts.note: at bridge East and North sit on opposing sides
to sue is to take legal action

explanation.surface: Pursue the rival card players and then take them to court.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow as a result, coming after in time, is a sense of go after.

clue.text: Decline to follow sun, wanting experience of shade

indicators.note: to follow means coming after, so this piece is placed later

parts.note: to age is to decline with years
green means inexperienced, a novice

explanation.surface: Growing old after too much sun, while still lacking experience of the shade.
explanation.definitionFit: A greyish green named after the herb's leaves is a colour, one particular shade.
